bigfoot.name: Ruby Creek incident
bigfoot.summary: According to a Skawahlook First Nation story, Jeannie Chapman and her three children saw a gigantic, hair-covered creature on their property near Ruby Creek and fled. Her husband George came home to find huge human-like footprints and a damaged woodshed. The family said it came back every night for a week, and they moved away for good.

ufo-saucer.name: Falcon Lake incident
ufo-saucer.summary: Prospector Stefan Michalak said a landed, metallic craft burned his chest when it lifted off. The RCMP, RCAF and Department of National Defence investigated; his burns were real, but his story shifted and later marks were judged self-inflicted. See the full case in Close encounters.

ufo-saucer.name: Langenburg saucers
ufo-saucer.summary: Farmer Edwin Fuhr said five spinning saucers hovered a foot above the ground by a slough, then shot away silently. The RCMP found five matching circles and no sign anyone had driven in to make them.

ufo-saucer.name: Clarenville sighting
ufo-saucer.summary: Early on October 26, twelve people reported an oval object with a fin hovering over the water near Random Island. RCMP Constable James Blackwood watched it for one to two hours through a surveillance telescope and said it flashed back when he shone his headlights at it. It left no physical evidence.

ufo-orbs.name: Petrozavodsk phenomenon
ufo-orbs.summary: Before dawn on September 20, a glowing object seemed to shower the Soviet city of Petrozavodsk with rays, and glowing objects were reported from Helsinki and Copenhagen to Vladivostok. It is often, though not universally, put down to the launch of the Kosmos-955 satellite. A Soviet Academy of Sciences report could not explain it, and the event helped start Setka, the Soviet research programme on anomalous phenomena.

ufo-orbs.name: Bonaventure Hotel lights
ufo-orbs.summary: On November 7, people at the rooftop pool of Montreal's Bonaventure Hotel watched 8 to 10 lights form a circle overhead and shine bright white rays for about three hours. La Presse and the CBC covered it, and no one identified the lights.
